The Endangered Species Act (ESA) establishes a comprehensive framework for the conservation of species that are threatened or endangered, along with the ecosystems upon which they depend. A central provision of the ESA mandates that all federal agencies must consult with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service or the National Marine Fisheries Service to ensure that any actions they authorize, fund, or carry out do not jeopardize the continued existence of any listed species or result in the destruction or adverse modification of designated critical habitat. This requirement, known as Section 7 consultation, is designed to prevent federal actions from contributing to the extinction of vulnerable species.

Regarding the specific question embedded in the text, the day that comes after Monday is Tuesday.
